title: When Webs Unite
logline: An old Ethiopian farmer on his sickbed calls his five quarrelling sons and, with a bundle of sticks, shows them that alone they break easily but together no one can break them.

characters.short: Abba Tesfaye: frail elderly Ethiopian Amhara man, long narrow face, high cheekbones, gaunt cheeks, straight narrow nose, deep-set dark eyes, medium-dark reddish-brown skin, short grey-white coiled hair and short white beard, white handwoven gabi shawl, small silver Orthodox cross

characters.short: the five sons: Ethiopian Amhara farmers aged 25 to 45, long oval faces, high cheekbones, straight narrow noses, warm reddish-brown skin, short black coiled hair; eldest bearded in a white gabi, second tall in a brown wool jacket, third moustached in a grey shirt, fourth with a tibeb-bordered netela scarf, youngest slim in a faded blue shirt

shots.reason: Establishing shot: the place and the one lit doorway lead us to the sickbed before we meet anyone.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme wide establishing shot at dusk of a small Amhara farming village: round houses with mud-plastered walls and conical grass-thatched roofs topped with a small clay pot, a stone-walled yard with a hedge of tall candelabra euphorbia cactus, two zebu oxen resting, terraced fields of golden teff and eucalyptus groves on the slopes, flat-topped amba mountains and escarpments on the horizon, a small round Orthodox church among dark juniper trees on a far hill; a deep blue evening sky with the last orange light; warm lamp light glowing from the open doorway of the nearest house. No people visible. Eye level, 24mm lens, deep focus

motion.video_prompt: slow cinematic pan to the right, evening mist drifts over the fields, the lamp light in the doorway flickers, nothing else moves

narration.en: In a village in the highlands, an old farmer, Abba Tesfaye, lay sick in his bed.
narration.spoken: በደጋው መንደር ውስጥ፣ አባ ተስፋዬ የሚባሉ አንድ አዛውንት ገበሬ ታመው በአልጋቸው ላይ ተኝተው ነበር።

shots.reason: Introduces the father and his worry in one image, so the audience asks what troubles him.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot at night inside a traditional round Amhara house: thick mud-and-straw plastered walls, a central wooden pole holding up the conical thatched roof, the inside of the thatch blackened by smoke. Abba Tesfaye lies propped up on a simple wooden alga bed strung with woven leather strips, his head on a folded cloth, a white gabi blanket pulled up to his chest, his thin hands resting on top of it; his eyes are open and worried, looking toward the doorway. A small kerosene lamp on a wooden stool beside the bed lights his face with warm orange light; behind him a built-in mud bench along the wall, a tall clay insira water jar, a woven mesob basket and a small wooden Orthodox cross hanging on the pole. Eye level, 50mm lens

narration.en: He knew his time was near. And one thing troubled him more than his illness.
narration.spoken: ጊዜያቸው እንደቀረበ ያውቁ ነበር። ከሕመማቸው በላይ ግን አንድ ነገር ያሳስባቸው ነበር።

shots.reason: Answers the question: the worry is the sons' division. Two groups and the oxen between them show what they fight over.
shots.image_prompt: Wide shot in late afternoon in the dusty yard of the family compound, enclosed by a low stone wall and a hedge of candelabra euphorbia: the five sons stand in two groups facing each other and argue; the second son and the third son point at each other with angry faces, the eldest stands with his arms crossed, the fourth shakes his head, the youngest turns away; between the two groups stand two zebu oxen with a wooden maresha plough and yoke; a round thatched house and eucalyptus trees behind them, teff fields and flat-topped mountains in the distance. Eye level, 28mm lens, all five faces visible

narration.en: His five sons were strong, but they always quarrelled: over the land, over the oxen, over everything.
narration.spoken: አምስቱ ልጆቻቸው ብርቱዎች ነበሩ፤ ግን ሁልጊዜ ይጣሉ ነበር፦ በመሬቱ፣ በበሬዎቹ፣ በሁሉም ነገር።

shots.reason: Brings the divided brothers into one frame for the first time, around their father.
shots.image_prompt: Medium wide shot at night inside a traditional round Amhara house: thick mud-and-straw plastered walls, a central wooden pole holding up the conical thatched roof, the inside of the thatch blackened by smoke: the five sons gather close around their father's wooden alga bed, faces lit by the warm kerosene lamp, serious and quiet; the eldest stands at the head of the bed, the youngest kneels on a sheepskin on the earth floor at the bedside, the other three stand behind near the central pole; Abba Tesfaye, propped up under the white gabi, looks at them. Eye level, 35mm lens, all six faces visible

narration.en: So he called all five of his sons to his bedside.
narration.spoken: ስለዚህ አምስቱንም ልጆቻቸውን ወደ አልጋቸው አጠገብ ጠሯቸው።

shots.reason: Introduces the object the whole lesson depends on; close so the tight cord is clearly seen.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up of Abba Tesfaye's frail wrinkled brown hands holding out a thick bundle of about ten straight wooden sticks, each as long as a forearm and as thick as a finger, tied tightly together in the middle with a leather cord; a strong younger hand reaches in from the side to take the bundle. The white gabi blanket below, warm lamp light, dark background, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, focus on the bundle and the cord

narration.en: He gave them a bundle of sticks, tied tightly together. 'Break it,' he said.
narration.spoken: በጥብቅ የታሰረ አንድ እስር እንጨት ሰጧቸው። «ስበሩት» አሉ።

shots.reason: Shows strength failing against the bundle, which sets up the surprise.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot inside a traditional round Amhara house: thick mud-and-straw plastered walls, a central wooden pole holding up the conical thatched roof, the inside of the thatch blackened by smoke, lit by a kerosene lamp: the eldest son, short black beard and white gabi on his shoulders, holds the tied bundle of sticks with both hands, one hand at each end, and presses it down hard over his raised knee, straining with effort; the bundle bends slightly but does not break; behind him the other four brothers watch, the second son reaching out to try next. 50mm lens

narration.en: One by one, each son tried with all his strength. No one could break it.
narration.spoken: አንድ በአንድ እያንዳንዱ ልጅ በሙሉ ኃይሉ ሞከረ። ማንም ሊሰብረው አልቻለም።

shots.reason: The turn: the same sticks, separated. The father's hands do the teaching.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up: Abba Tesfaye, sitting up in bed, holds the untied leather cord in his left hand and with his right hand gives a single wooden stick to the youngest son, whose open hand reaches for it; the other loose sticks lie across the white gabi on his lap. Warm lamp light, 85mm lens, focus on the father's face and the single stick

narration.en: Then he untied the bundle and gave each son a single stick. 'Now break yours.'
narration.spoken: ከዚያም እስሩን ፈትተው ለእያንዳንዱ ልጅ አንድ አንድ እንጨት ሰጡ። «አሁን የራሳችሁን ስበሩ።»

shots.reason: The surprise, shown with all five at once so the audience sees it before it is explained.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot inside a traditional round Amhara house: thick mud-and-straw plastered walls, a central wooden pole holding up the conical thatched roof, the inside of the thatch blackened by smoke: the five brothers stand side by side near the alga bed, each holding one single thin wooden stick with both hands and snapping it in half at the same moment, small splinters in the air, their faces surprised and thoughtful. Warm kerosene lamp light, 35mm lens, all five faces visible

motion.video_prompt: the five men snap their sticks in half, small splinters fly, then they look at the broken pieces, static camera

shots.reason: The father's words name the lesson; the brothers touching each other already show them taking it in.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up: Abba Tesfaye propped up in bed speaks softly with a calm, loving face, his right hand resting on the tied bundle of sticks lying on the white gabi; the youngest son kneels at the bedside holding his father's left hand, the eldest son's hand rests on the youngest's shoulder, the other brothers' listening faces at the edge of the frame. Warm lamp light, 50mm lens

narration.en: 'My sons,' he said, 'alone, you are like one stick. Together, no one can break you.'
narration.spoken: «ልጆቼ» አሉ፤ «ብቻችሁን ስትሆኑ እንደ አንድ እንጨት ናችሁ። አንድ ስትሆኑ ግን ማንም ሊሰብራችሁ አይችልም።»

shots.reason: Resolution: the quarrel of s03 becomes shared work in the same fields, and the proverb gives the moral a local voice.
shots.image_prompt: Wide shot at sunrise in the terraced highland fields below the village: the five brothers work together; the second and third sons guide a pair of zebu oxen pulling a wooden maresha plough through red-brown earth, the fourth scatters teff seed from a woven basket, the eldest and the youngest carry one heavy eucalyptus log together on their shoulders; behind them the round thatched family house beside a euphorbia hedge, with the tied bundle of sticks hanging beside its doorway, and flat-topped amba mountains in morning mist. Golden morning light, eye level, 28mm lens

motion.video_prompt: the oxen pull the plough slowly forward, seed falls from the basket, the two brothers walk with the log, morning mist, slow camera

narration.en: From that day, the brothers worked as one. As the elders say: when spider webs unite, they can tie up a lion.
narration.spoken: ከዚያ ቀን ጀምሮ ወንድማማቾቹ እንደ አንድ ሰው ሠሩ። አበው እንዳሉት፦ ድር ቢያብር አንበሳ ያስር።
